problem: Most indoor robot navigation systems rely on geometric maps (laser scanners, range-finders, radar) and lack scene understanding. Semantic navigation systems combine geometry-based and vision-based components, and no comprehensive review or common evaluation criteria for them exists.
motivation: A semantic model of the indoor environment is closer to human perception, so it can improve navigation and human-robot interaction. Because semantic navigation needs several interacting components, a critical review and a standard set of evaluation metrics are needed to compare systems.
key_idea: Review and critically analyze recent indoor robot semantic navigation systems, and propose a set of evaluation metrics for assessing any such system.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analysis are visible. The abstract's main claim is that semantic navigation depends on combining geometry-based and vision-based components, so systems should be judged on both.
method: Literature review: surveys recently developed robot semantic navigation systems for indoor environments.
Critical analysis: examines each system's use of geometry-based and vision-based components for semantic navigation.
Evaluation metrics: proposes a set of metrics for assessing the efficiency of any robot semantic navigation system.
results: This is a survey with no experimental results. Its contribution is a review and critical analysis of indoor semantic navigation systems plus a proposed set of evaluation metrics.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the coverage, taxonomy and details of the proposed metrics could not be assessed.
As a 2023 survey, it likely predates the LLM/VLM-based navigation wave.
